Whether /api/v1/search/ accepts any structure query at all — InChI, InChIKey, SMILES, formula or compound name. The map documents only solvent/temperature/nucleus filters. If no chemical-identity query exists there is no molecule-to-record entry point, and nothing downstream matters for NMRx's primary use case.

If a structure query exists, whether it matches exactly with stereochemistry, charge and isotope preserved, or only fuzzily by name. The map forbids silently merging salts, stereoisomers and tautomers, so a loose matcher needs a downstream identity check before use.

Whether any nmrXiv record exposes per-atom assignments in machine-readable form (for example NMReDATA or an assignment table), and what fraction do. The map warns explicitly that raw data plus acquisition metadata does not imply an assigned spectrum. This one unknown decides calibration eligibility.

Whether spectrometer frequency and the referencing compound/method appear in the record payload. Solvent, temperature and nucleus are documented as filters; the other two conditions NMRx tracks are undocumented for this source and must not be filled in by assumption.

Whether measurements are retrievable as numerical values (peak lists, shift tables) or only as raw/processed instrument files that NMRx would have to process locally — which would add an FID-processing dependency to the adapter.

The exact host serving raw files and BagIt archives. The map states it may differ from nmrxiv.org, so that hostname must be resolved from a real download link before any allowlist request; permitting the portal alone may not permit file retrieval.

Whether the per-project/per-sample license is a structured field in the API response, what values occur, and whether propagation to child spectra is machine-readable. Rights cannot be taken from the site footer, so a record-level license field is the only viable gate.

Whether metadata access or downloads require authentication or an account for any record class, and any published rate limit. Neither file states nmrXiv's auth posture (contrast Chemotion, where the map flags registration for some dataset downloads).

Whether nmrXiv deposits duplicate records already held from Chemotion, BMRB metabolomics or nmrshiftdb2, and which stable identifier (DOI or dataset ID) supports deduplication without destroying source lineage.

Whether the documented /api/v1/search/ prefix is current and complete — it is a path fragment quoted in secondary research, not a schema read from the provider, so the full route, verb and required parameters must be confirmed against the API documentation rather than guessed.
notes: The only source with documented search filters for solvent, temperature and nucleus. Raw data plus acquisition metadata does NOT guarantee an assigned spectrum. Licences are per project/sample and propagate to spectra; do not read them off the footer.
